newsitem.title: GERMANY: German government rebuffs talk of EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: German government rebuffs talk of EMU delay.

text.p: Rebuffing suggestions that Europe's monetary union should be delayed, the German government restated on Monday its belief that the single currency project must go foward as planned in 1999.
Government spokesman Peter Hausmann said that delaying European economic and monetary union (EMU) would jeopardise it altogether.
Hausmann also restated the government's view that monetary union would start on schedule and that the future European currency, the euro, will be stable.

The spokesman made his remarks after Saxony state premier Kurt Biedenkopf was quoted over the weekend as saying there was no rush to start EMU and he could imagine delaying the start for five years to allow aspiring members to improve their economies.
Biedenkopf is a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling Christian Democrats (CDU).
